deferred_follow_up: Process-level tool-server isolation remains DEFERRED-FOLLOW-UP. Real mutation evidence closes hosted-kernel and portable verified-core capability mediation for tool-name and server-ID pivots. The same in-tree test exercises WASM host-import and fuel containment, but those WASM assertions do not yet carry a promoted targeted cargo-mutants transcript. Chio does not sandbox arbitrary in-process connector code, and the test does not exercise malformed authenticated transport framing across a separate process. Follow-up work must add targeted WASM mutation evidence, a process-boundary transport test, and operational evidence for OS or container sandboxing, least-privilege filesystem access, and outbound-network restrictions.
note: Real partial mutation evidence. The conformance test at crates/tooling/chio-conformance/tests/threats/tool_server_escape.rs exercises three production boundaries. The hosted-kernel test registers deliberately permissive attacker-controlled ToolServerConnection implementations, proves an admitted control call reaches one connection, then proves tool-name and server-ID privilege pivots are denied before either connection is invoked. The portable verified-core path applies the same positive and negative controls. Targeted cargo-mutants runs forced chio-kernel::request_matching::grant_matches_request and chio-kernel-core::scope::grant_covers to return Ok(true); the conformance test caught both complete scope bypasses. WasmtimeBackend host-import and fuel assertions also pass, but are not promoted as mutation-backed coverage here. PARTIAL: targeted WASM mutation evidence, authenticated process transport, and operator-enforced OS or container isolation remain deferred.
